contract: Transaction and block inventories reject duplicate hashes and unsupported types and are ignored until both synchronization directions complete.
Fetches correlate to advertised inventory or the peer sync window; advertisement and sync block paths are distinguished before validation.
Pending inventory is bounded at 100000, transaction payload cache at 50000 for one hour, block cache at 10 for one minute, and spread queues at 1000.

Java-compatible ten-second inventory windows accept at most maxTps*10 transaction hashes and maxBlockInvPerSecond*10 block hashes; duplicate, per-message, and rate validation completes before any cache or provider insertion.

Per-peer received/spread inventories are bounded at 20000 entries with one-hour expiry; global provider state has deterministic entry and byte backpressure, one-hour expiry, and removes empty keys on disconnect.
Requests stale at 15 seconds, advertisement requests time out at 20 seconds, and blocks older than 3 seconds are not spread.

The provider with the fewest outstanding requests is selected with address tie-breaking; transaction order is retained, blocks spread by ascending height, disconnects requeue only with another provider.
Transaction IDs and Java advertisement correlation hash the exact preserved Transaction.raw_data wire bytes, independent of signatures and results.
Transaction responses split at 1000000 serialized bytes and block responses contain exactly one block.
